chunks.title: CLO Tips Workshop - Adding Seam Allowance
chunks.content: ## Adding Fonts in CLO: Importing and Displaying Font Information This section explains how to import font data from .dxf files into CLO and how to display and verify font information within the software, focusing on font conversion and display settings. To add fonts in CLO, start by importing a .dxf file. In the import pop-up window, select the option to convert the .dxf font information into CLO fonts. Once imported, the font details will appear in the window. If the font does not display normally, check the 2D window display menu. Open the display settings to find options for normal font display. This ensures the font information from the .dxf file is rendered correctly in the workspace. For example, when working with a sleeve pattern, verify the font information on the right side panel. If some fonts are not correctly recognized, CLO allows you to add and correct these fonts manually. --- ## Editing and Adding Fonts Using the Font Tool in CLO This section covers the use of the Font Tool in the 2D toolbar to add and modify fonts, including adjusting font properties like type, width, and seam type. To add font data manually: 1. Open the 2D toolbar and select the font tool. 2. Click once on the desired location to add the font. 3. Add fonts on either of the two outside pages available in the workspace. In the Property Editor, you can then modify: - Font type - Font width - Seam type For example, when working on a sleeve pattern, select the font section and use the Property Editor to adjust settings appropriate to the garment’s craftsmanship. --- ## Adjusting Cross-Point Connection Methods for Fonts This section explains how to modify the cross-point connection style in font segments, an important detail for garment construction precision. To adjust the cross-point connection: 1. Select the font section you want to modify. 2. In the Property Editor, find the cross-point connection method. 3. Set the cross-point connection to the desired type (e.g., second type out of six available). Test different connection types as needed since the correct choice depends on the actual sewing method and garment construction requirements. --- ## Creating Uneven Seam Widths in CLO Patterns This section details how to create seams with varying widths along a single line segment, using CLO’s seam editing features. To create uneven seam widths: 1. Select the line or seam you want to edit. 2. In the Property Editor, change the seam type from the default “line” (uniform width) to “point.” 3. This allows you to set different seam widths at each end of the line segment. For example, you can set one end of the seam width to 10 mm, and the other end to a different width, enabling precise seam allowance control. --- ## Editing Seam Openings and Widths This section explains how to modify seam openings and overall seam widths to match design and construction specifications.
